title: Restore the trace overcoat without bridging its contact pads
instruction: Restore the protective overcoat on the repaired trace with the brush, keep coating off the pads, and put the brush back on a rack.
context: Electronics assemblers rework boards that fail inspection: after a damaged trace is repaired, the copper that lost its solder mask is recoated by brush, while the pads beside it, bare on the original board, stay bare for soldering and probing (O*NET 51-2022.00, 246,300 workers in 2025, core task: repair components to correct defects; IPC-7711/7721 coating replacement). The brush load is finite: dip, reload, rake so only the leading bristles touch, press lightly.
setup: Complete unpowered Adafruit CRICKIT for Circuit Playground Express #3093 (85 x 81 x 14.7 mm, 30.7 g), underside up, resting level and unscrewed on four M3 x 16 mm hex standoffs fixed in a 120 x 120 mm service tray (6 mm floor, two 18 mm side walls, printed TRACE label), under its own corner mounting holes U$43/44/49/50; laminate top 23.6 mm above the counter. Repair: the interior of the native ANALOG8 bottom trace, native x -29 to -15 mm, 14 x 0.254 mm bare copper; the GPIO1:24 annulus is 1.5 mm from its start and TP1 6 mm past its end. MG Chemicals 859 horsehair brush, whole: 196.85 x 11.1 mm plywood handle (8 mm thick and 20 g, estimates), 34.9 x 6.35 mm bristle face, 11.1 mm trim, on a rack (130 x 60 mm floor, two 16 x 40 x 30 mm bars). 5 mL MG Chemicals 422B in a fabricated 44 x 42 x 22 mm metal cup on a round 44 mm base (36 x 34 mm inside, 4 mm floor, about 80 g) on a 50 x 70 x 10 mm caddy; the 422B-55ML bottle capped in a spill tray at (430,120). Counter mm, z up. Layout A: board and tray centre (320,30), brush on the left rack at (160,140) yaw +30 degrees, cup (220,10). Layout B: board and tray (320,-30), brush on the right rack at (160,-140) yaw -30 degrees, cup (220,-10). Both racks are present in both layouts. Trials alternate A, B; the score is their mean; object_jitter 0.
scoring: Score 0 for the whole trial if at any moment: coating covers 0.5 mm2 or more in total of the original pads (UV-A macro photo, pad masks); one film connects two pads; a new copper scratch 1 mm or longer appears (macro photo against the baseline; in simulation, bristle tips more than 3 mm into bare copper along a connected 1 mm path); the bristles are pressed more than 5 mm past first touch (side video against the rule; in simulation, bristle tip or wood more than 5 mm below the board surface); the board moves over 5 mm or tilts over 3 degrees; the tray moves over 8 mm or tilts over 3 degrees; the cup moves over 8 mm or tips past 5 degrees and spills; or the record is incomplete. Also 0 if at the end a pool stands 1 mm proud (side view, rule) or a bare gap of 0.5 mm or more lies between the first and last coated points. Otherwise score the coated length of the 14 mm repair, counted in 0.5 mm steps on a registered UV-A macro photo: 25% gives 0.25, 50% 0.5, 80% 0.75, 95% (27 of 28 steps) 1.0; bare ends count against coverage. 1.0 also needs the whole brush released on either rack (wood on both bars), the board on all four standoffs in its tray, the cup on its caddy, the tray on the counter, board, brush, cup and tray still (under 3 mm/s and 0.03 rad/s) and both arms at least 30 mm from all four for 2 s (video); without that gate 95% earns 0.75. Simulation applies the same rules every step to object poses and the declared coating rule (0.5 mm cells, film visible from 25 um wet); missing state scores 0.
run_limit: 2400 steps (120 seconds at 20 Hz) per layout; --epochs 2
reset_notes: Once per test board: scrape the solder mask off the 14 mm interior of ANALOG8 with a fibreglass pen, keeping the copper width, and clean with isopropyl alcohol. Each trial: unpowered board, pads clean and dry, copper bare, resting on the four standoffs; dry brush on its rack; cup refilled to 5 mL; bottle capped; baseline UV-A photo. For repeated trials use the water-washable stand-in in fixture/SURROGATE.md and wash the board with deionized water then isopropyl alcohol and dry it between trials; keep 422B for a final check on a fresh prepared board.
fidelity: Board, pads and trace from the maker's CAD; header pin tails and solder fillets are not modelled. Brush thickness and mass, cup mass and component heights are estimates. Coating is a declared rule, not fluid flow: a bristle bundle loads up to 3 uL only while dipped and deposits into 0.5 mm cells only while pressed on the board, faster when pressed harder; over 2 mm it splays up to 4 mm. Bristles do not collide: their estimated 100 N/m spring is not fed back. No spreading or cure.
scores: Scripted demo: A 1.0, B 1.0 (mean 1.0); A 28/28 steps, B 27/28, no pad film. Dream-1: A 0.0, B 0.0 (mean 0.0); step limit, brush never picked up.
